key_points: Supported opcodes: 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C
Get Log Page: success status with DW0 = 9 and no data
AER: slot released, never completed
Unsupported opcode -> ASSERT -> infinite loop
Only CNS bit 0 is decoded

question: Which NVM I/O commands are supported, and what happens if the host sends Dataset Management (TRIM), Write Zeroes, Compare or Write Uncorrectable?
answer: Only Flush (0x00, completed immediately with success and no flushing), Write (0x01) and Read (0x02) (both go to ReqTransNvmeToSlice). Any other opcode prints 'Not Support IO Command OPC: %X' and ASSERT(0) -> infinite loop: the firmware hangs and the command never completes. Identify advertises ONCS = 0 (no Compare, Write Uncorrectable or DSM), so a compliant host should not send them; TRIM/unmap is not implemented at all (LSAs are never unmapped). For Read/Write the FUA bit (its check is commented out), DSM hints (DW13), PRINFO and LR are ignored, and NSID is not checked.
key_points: Supported: Flush, Write, Read
Flush is a no-op success
Any other opcode -> ASSERT hang
ONCS = 0; no TRIM; FUA ignored

question: What key values does the firmware return in Identify Controller and Identify Namespace, and how is the Identify data transferred?
answer: Controller: VID = SSVID = 0x1EDC; SN 'SSDD515T', MN 'Cosmos+ OpenSSD', FR 'TYPE0005' (space-padded, but memcpy with sizeof also copies the terminating NUL into SN/MN, and FR's NUL spills into RAB which is then set to 0); IEEE OUI E4 D2 5C; MDTS = 8 (1 MiB maximum transfer with 4 KiB pages); CNTLID = 9; OACS = 0; ACL = 3; AERL = 3; FRMW: slot 1 read-only, 1 slot; LPA = 0; ELPE = 8; NPSS = 0; SQES = 0x66 (64 B); CQES = 0x44 (16 B); NN = 1; ONCS = 0; FUSES = 0; FNA = 0; VWC present = 1; SGL unsupported; PSD0 MP = 0x09C4 (25.00 W). Namespace: NSZE = NCAP = NUSE = storageCapacity_L (upper dword 0); no thin provisioning; NLBAF = 0 (single format); FLBAS = 0; LBAF0: MS = 0, LBADS = 12 (4,096-byte LBAs), RP = 2; no metadata or protection. The data is built at 0x00200000 and sent with direct Tx DMA: the PRP1 part up to the 4 KiB boundary, the remainder via PRP2, then a busy-wait for DMA completion.
key_points: VID/SSVID 0x1EDC; MN 'Cosmos+ OpenSSD'
MDTS 8, SQES 0x66, CQES 0x44
NN 1, ONCS 0, VWC present
LBADS 12 (4 KiB), NLBAF 0, MS 0
NSZE = NCAP = NUSE = storageCapacity_L

question: What queue-management limits and feature handling does the firmware implement (Create I/O SQ/CQ checks, Set/Get Features)?
answer: Up to 8 I/O SQs and 8 I/O CQs (MAX_NUM_OF_IO_SQ/CQ = 8; QID 1..8 stored at index QID-1). Create I/O SQ asserts PRP1 low 4 bits == 0 and PRP1 high dword < 0x10, 0 < QID <= 8, QSIZE < 0x100 (<= 256 entries) and 0 < CQID <= 8, then programs the hardware SQ register (base, valid, cqVector = CQID, size). Create I/O CQ asserts an aligned PRP1, IV < 8, QSIZE < 0x100 and 0 < QID <= 8, then programs base, valid, irqEn = IEN, irqVector = IV, size. Only physically contiguous queues are supported (PC is not checked); delete clears the registers. Set Features: Number of Queues (FID 7) -> DW0 echoes NSQR/NCQR each clamped to 7 (max 8 queues); Arbitration (1), Power Management (2), Interrupt Coalescing (8), Async Event Configuration (0x0B) -> accepted and ignored; VWC (6) -> cacheEn. Get Features: LBA Range Type (3) -> status Invalid Field in Command (asserts NSID == 1); Temperature Threshold (4) -> returns DW11; VWC -> cacheEn; Power Management -> 0. Any other FID (e.g. Get Number of Queues, Set Temperature Threshold, Error Recovery) -> ASSERT hang. The admin queue is enabled by the firmware writing the admin-queue register when CC.EN becomes 1.
key_points: 8 I/O SQs + 8 I/O CQs; QSIZE < 256, IV < 8, PRP 16-byte aligned
Set Number of Queues clamps NSQR/NCQR to 7
Supported Set FIDs: 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 0x0B; Get FIDs: 2, 3, 4, 6
Get LBA Range Type returns Invalid Field in Command
Unsupported FID -> ASSERT hang

question: How are host data transfers performed for Read/Write, how does the firmware detect their completion, and who generates the NVMe completion?
answer: IssueNvmeDmaReq issues one auto DMA per 4 KiB NVMe block of the slice request: set_auto_rx_dma (host -> device, for writes) or set_auto_tx_dma (device -> host, for reads) with (cmdSlotTag, cmd4KBOffset = startIndex + i, devAddr = 0x10000000 + entry x 16 KiB + (nvmeBlockOffset + i) x 4 KiB, autoCompletion = 1). Only devAddr and the control word are written; the hardware derives the host address from the command's PRPs using the 4 KiB offset (asserted < 256). The auto Rx and Tx DMA command FIFOs have 256 entries: the firmware spins while (tail + 1) % 256 == head (head read from HOST_DMA_FIFO_CNT). After issuing, the request records reqTail = the software FIFO tail and overFlowCnt = the number of 8-bit tail wrap-arounds. CheckDoneNvmeDmaReq walks the NVMe DMA queue from tail (newest) to head; for the first Rx (resp. Tx) request whose recorded tail has been passed by the hardware head (check_auto_*_dma_partial_done, wrap-aware via the overflow count), that request and all older Rx (resp. Tx) requests are considered done and freed (the DMA engine completes in order). The NVMe CQ entry for Read/Write is produced by the hardware when all auto-completion DMAs of the command have finished. Admin data (Identify) instead uses direct DMA with an explicit PCIe address and length (<= 4 KiB, 16-byte aligned) and busy-waits.
key_points: One auto DMA per 4 KiB with slot tag, 4 KiB offset and DRAM address
DMA FIFO depth 256; firmware spins when full
Completion detection via recorded FIFO tail + overflow count compared with the hardware head
A finished newer request implies older same-direction requests are finished
NVMe completion for I/O generated by hardware auto-completion

question: What happens if a Read/Write has a start LBA >= the advertised capacity, a non-zero upper LBA dword, a range running past the end of the namespace, or a transfer larger than 1 MiB?
answer: handle_nvme_io_read/write ASSERT that startLba[0] < storageCapacity_L and startLba[1] == 0 (STORAGE_CAPACITY_H = 0), that the PRP1/PRP2 low dwords are 16-byte aligned and that the PRP high dwords are < 0x10. A failing ASSERT prints 'error in <file>: Line <n>' and loops forever - no LBA Out of Range (or any other) error completion is returned. Only the start LBA is checked: a range that starts inside the namespace but extends past its end is processed normally (slices above the exported capacity but below SLICES_PER_SSD are mapped like any other; an LSA >= SLICES_PER_SSD would hit the FTL assert). The NLB limit check (MAX_NUM_OF_NLB) is commented out, but every auto DMA asserts cmd4KBOffset < 256, so a transfer of more than 256 x 4 KiB = 1 MiB (beyond MDTS = 8) hangs the firmware.
key_points: Start LBA >= capacity or upper LBA dword != 0 -> ASSERT -> infinite loop
No NVMe error status is ever returned
The end of the range is not checked
More than 256 blocks (1 MiB) trips the cmd4KBOffset < 256 assert

question: How does the firmware receive NVMe commands from the host-interface hardware and post completions?
answer: The NVMe IP fetches SQ entries itself. The firmware polls NVME_CMD_FIFO_REG (IP base + 0x300): bit31 cmdValid, bits[3:0] qID, bits[14:8] cmdSlotTag (7 bits -> 128 slots), bits[23:16] cmdSeqNum. The 64-byte command is read as 16 dwords from NVME_CMD_SRAM (base + 0x2000) + slotTag x 64. Completions go to NVME_CPL_FIFO (base + 0x304): auto completion (cplType 1) writes DW0 'specific' to +4 and {cmdSlotTag[6:0], cplType[15:14], status field[31:16]} to +8 - the hardware supplies CID/SQID from the slot; slot release (cplType 2) frees a slot without a CQ entry (used for AER); cplType 0 (completion only) writes sqId/cid explicitly (an unused path). Read/Write completions are posted by DMA auto-completion; Flush and admin commands by set_auto_nvme_cpl. Status field word: bit0 reserved (phase), SC bits[8:1], SCT bits[11:9], M bit14, DNR bit15.
key_points: Poll the command FIFO register: valid bit, qID, 7-bit slot tag, sequence number
Command dwords read from command SRAM at slotTag x 64
Completion FIFO types: auto completion by slot tag (1), slot release (2), explicit completion (0)
Status field layout: SC bits 8:1, SCT bits 11:9

question: In what order does InitFTL initialize the subsystems, and why must the request/scheduler layers be initialized before the address map?
answer: CheckConfigRestriction -> InitChCtlReg (chCtlReg[ch] = NSC_ch_BASEADDR) -> InitReqPool (pool pointer, all requests in the free queue, all queues empty, counters 0) -> InitDependencyTable (row-address table zeroed) -> InitReqScheduler (table pointers, all ways idle, retry limits 5, flags 0) -> InitNandArray (RESET + SET_FEATURE to every die, then sync) -> InitAddressMap (phyBlockMap identity, BBT block 0, first allocation die, slice maps cleared, InitBlockDieMap) -> InitDataBuf (LRU/hash/temp buffers) -> InitGcVictimMap (all buckets empty) -> storageCapacity_L computed and printed. NAND reset, BBT read/scan/save and block erasure are performed through the regular request pool, dependency check and scheduler (SelectLowLevelReqQ + SyncAllLowLevelReqDone), so those layers must exist first. InitFTL runs inside nvme_main before the host is told to start ('Turn on the host PC').
key_points: Order: config check, NSC registers, request pool, dependency table, scheduler, NAND reset, address map, data buffer, GC victim map, capacity
NAND/BBT initialization uses the normal request and scheduler machinery
Capacity is computed last (it needs the bad-block count)

question: Describe the boot-time block initialization (InitBlockDieMap), including the operator prompt.
answer: It prints "Press 'X' to re-make the bad block table." and blocks in inbyte() until a character arrives on the UART console. If it is 'X', EraseTotalBlockSpace erases every physical block 0..8367 of every die (PHY_ORG, total space - including BBT blocks and factory-bad blocks) and eraseFlag = 0. Then: InitDieMap (empty free lists); RecoverBadBlockTable(RESERVED_DATA_BUFFER_BASE_ADDR): read each die's BBT (block 0, page 1), load it if its first byte is 0 or 1, otherwise scan the factory marks (FindBadBlock) and save new tables (SaveBadBlockTable); clear grownBadUpdate. Then mark each die's BBT block bad in phyBlockMap; RemapBadBlock; InitBlockMap (virtual block bad flags, free = 1, counters 0, eraseCnt 0, good blocks appended to the free list); if eraseFlag is still 1 (i.e. 'X' was not pressed) EraseUserBlockSpace erases every good user virtual block (VSA addressing, no dependency check); finally InitCurrentBlockOfDieMap takes one free block per die as the current block (assert if none).
key_points: Boot blocks on UART inbyte(); 'X' erases the whole array and forces a BBT rebuild
RecoverBadBlockTable: read, validate, scan and save as needed
BBT block masked as bad, then remap and block-map initialization
All good user blocks are erased at every normal boot
One current block per die taken from the free list

question: After a power cycle (even following a clean NVMe shutdown), which host data is still readable and which FTL state is recovered from flash?
answer: None of the host data. The only persistent FTL structure is the per-die bad block table (physical block 0, page 1). The L2P/P2L slice maps, block/die metadata (invalid counts, free lists, erase counts), GC lists and the data buffer exist only in DRAM and are never saved; no LSA or other metadata is written into the page spare area (the 256-byte spare buffers are never filled by the FTL), so the maps could not be rebuilt by scanning either. At every boot InitSliceMap marks all LSAs unmapped and InitBlockDieMap erases every good user block (EraseUserBlockSpace, or the whole array if 'X' is pressed). Dirty write-back data still in DRAM at power-off is lost as well. Reads after a reboot therefore return stale/uninitialized buffer contents for every LBA.
key_points: Only the bad block table persists on NAND
Maps and block metadata are DRAM-only and never saved
No LSA/OOB metadata is written to the spare area, so no rebuild by scan
All good user blocks are erased at every boot; all host data is lost
